description: Essential knowledge for personal finance, budgeting, investing, and financial planning

budgeting.50_30_20_rule: 50% needs, 30% wants, 20% savings and debt repayment
budgeting.zero_based: Every dollar assigned a purpose; income minus expenses = zero
budgeting.emergency_fund: 3–6 months of expenses in liquid, accessible account

banking.checking_account: For daily transactions; typically no interest
banking.savings_account: Earn interest; higher APY = more growth
banking.high_yield_savings: Online banks often offer 4–5% APY vs 0.01% at traditional banks
banking.compound_interest: Interest earned on principal plus previously earned interest; grows exponentially
banking.compound_formula: A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt); A=amount, P=principal, r=rate, n=times/year, t=years

debt_management.good_vs_bad_debt: Good: investments in assets that appreciate (mortgage, student loans); Bad: high-interest consumer debt
debt_management.debt_avalanche: Pay minimums on all; extra payment to highest-interest debt first; saves most money
debt_management.debt_snowball: Pay minimums on all; extra payment to smallest balance; psychological wins
debt_management.credit_utilization: Keep below 30% of credit limit to maintain good credit score

investing_fundamentals.risk_vs_return: Higher potential return typically comes with higher risk
investing_fundamentals.diversification: Spread investments across asset classes to reduce risk

asset_classes.stocks: Ownership shares in companies; highest long-term growth potential
asset_classes.bonds: Debt instruments; lower risk/return than stocks
asset_classes.real_estate: Physical property or REITs; income + appreciation
asset_classes.cash_equivalents: Money market funds, T-bills; very low risk/return
asset_classes.commodities: Gold, oil, agricultural products; inflation hedge

investing_fundamentals.index_funds: Track market index (S&P 500); low fees; outperform most active managers long-term
investing_fundamentals.dollar_cost_averaging: Invest fixed amounts at regular intervals; reduces timing risk
investing_fundamentals.rule_of_72: Divide 72 by interest rate to estimate years to double money (72/7% = ~10 years)

retirement_accounts.401k_403b: Employer-sponsored; pre-tax contributions lower taxable income; employer match is free money
retirement_accounts.traditional_ira: Pre-tax contributions; tax-deferred growth; taxed on withdrawal
retirement_accounts.roth_ira: After-tax contributions; tax-free growth and withdrawal; income limits apply
retirement_accounts.order_of_operations: 1. 401k to employer match → 2. Pay high-interest debt → 3. Max HSA → 4. Max Roth IRA → 5. Max 401k → 6. Taxable brokerage

insurance.life: Income replacement for dependents; term vs whole life
insurance.health: Medical expenses; high-deductible plan + HSA often optimal
insurance.auto: Required by law; liability + collision + comprehensive
insurance.disability: Often overlooked; replaces income if unable to work

taxes.marginal_vs_effective: Marginal = rate on last dollar earned; Effective = average rate paid

capital_gains.short_term: Assets held < 1 year; taxed as ordinary income
